title: evaluation.json
description: TeA's manifest for one Evaluate evaluation folder. The tea-evaluate runtime owns this schema. The top level is closed, so each later field is an additive schema change with its own check cases.

schemaVersion.description: The evaluation.json format version. tea-evaluate check refuses a version the installed runtime does not know before it validates anything else.

evaluationId.description: Kebab-case identifier; the evaluation folder is named after it.

targetKind.description: What is evaluated (AD-4). Recorded only here, never in a contract.

interface.description: The interface kind the contract declares. A web application maps to api; web is never emitted.

registry.description: The execution-target registry: every command a run may spawn (a RegistryEntry) and every stdio MCP tool server it may start (an McpRegistryEntry, kind mcp). The runtime builds eval-quality's default-deny CommandTargetPolicy and McpTargetPolicy from these entries for the workspace each call runs in, so a target the registry does not name is denied before a process starts.

launch.description: Where the target lives, which every launch resolves against.

root.description: The evaluated project's root, relative to the evaluation folder: POSIX, "." and ".." segments allowed so it can climb out of the folder, never absolute, with no empty segment, no trailing slash, and no control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character. Registry targets, the skill root and every mutation's targetArtifact resolve against it, and tea-evaluate preflight runs its arms and legs in disposable workspaces made from it.

skillRoot.description: The skill directory, holding SKILL.md, relative to root: the --skill-root tea-skill-runner receives. Required when targetKind is skill; tea-evaluate check refuses a mutation whose targetArtifact is not inside it. POSIX and relative, with no drive letter, no "." or ".." segment, no empty segment, no trailing slash, and no control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character.

workspace.description: The disposable workspace a run and a mutation happen in (AD-8). The runtime writes nothing into the adopter's tree; a target that writes outside its workspace is detected and the run exits 12.

kind.description: git: a detached worktree at the evaluated commit (HEAD) when launch.root is in a git repository, and a temp copy otherwise. copy: a temp copy identified by its tree digest. tea-evaluate preflight --from-working-tree makes a temp copy of the working tree whatever the kind, and records the run as dirty.

provision.description: Relative directories copied into every workspace from the target (for example node_modules, which a worktree lacks) with their write bits removed, so a leg can read one and cannot write it. A mutation may not target a file inside one. Each is POSIX and relative, with no drive letter, no "." or ".." segment, no empty segment, and no control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character, so none can name the whole target; a trailing slash is allowed.

arms.description: The condition arms a run executes: clean for the clean controls, mutated for the controlled-mutation probes (one arm per mutation), historical for the historical probes (one arm per pre-fix revision) and gameability for the gameability probes (one arm per probe, launching nothing).

judge.description: The rubric judge tea-evaluate run calls once per trial when the contract declares a rubric and the evaluator is the deterministic one, through TeA's agent adapters; tea-evaluate check requires it then, and requires policy/evaluator-conditions.json to name the judge's model snapshot. Under any other evaluator kind the evaluator scores the rubric, so no judge is called and check refuses this block as unused; a contract with no rubric makes no judge call whatever this says.

agent.description: The agent adapter the judge runs through, by its key in TeA's adapter table; tea-evaluate check refuses a key the table does not hold.

agentCommand.description: The executable to run in place of the adapter's default command; the custom adapter has none and requires it.

agentArgs.description: Arguments appended after the adapter's own argv; the custom adapter's whole argv.

model.description: The model the adapter runs, in place of its pinned default; an adapter with no model flag refuses one.

timeoutMs.description: The wall clock one judge call gets, in milliseconds; a judge still running then is stopped, and the trial yields no record.

evaluator.description: The evaluation layer that judges every scored trial (AD-21). Absent, the run judges with the deterministic evaluator. Each kind reaches eval-quality score as sealed run records: deterministic resolves each oracle with eval-quality's resolveCheck; command runs an adopter executable under evaluator/ once per trial and converts the judgment rows it prints through evaluator/mapping.json; sealed-brief-agent runs an agent through TeA's agent adapters on the sealed brief alone, acting on the target only through the runtime's MCP bridge, and converts its judgment rows the same way; records takes the sealed run records an adopter harness wrote and passes them to score unchanged.

kind.description: Which evaluation layer judges the trials.

command.description: command: the executable the runtime starts once per trial, a POSIX path under evaluator/ (relative to the evaluation folder, with no "." or ".." segment), so the evaluator tree digest covers it. It must be a regular executable file; it receives { sealedBrief, observations } on stdin and prints { rows, recommendation? } on stdout.

args.description: command: arguments the executable receives, in order.

environmentKeys.description: command and sealed-brief-agent: environment keys passed from the host to the evaluator beside the base set (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, locale and proxy variables, and a built-in agent adapter's own credential variables), such as a model credential a model-graded evaluator or a custom agent needs. PATH is in the base set already.

timeoutMs.description: command and sealed-brief-agent: the wall clock one trial's evaluator gets, in milliseconds; an evaluator still running then has its process group stopped, and the trial yields no record (exit 12).

agent.description: sealed-brief-agent: the agent adapter the evaluator runs through, by its key in TeA's adapter table; tea-evaluate check refuses one that cannot run with the bridge as its only tools.

agentCommand.description: sealed-brief-agent: the executable to run in place of the adapter's default command; the custom adapter has none and requires it.

agentArgs.description: sealed-brief-agent: arguments appended after the adapter's own argv; the custom adapter's whole argv, before the --mcp-config the runtime adds.

model.description: sealed-brief-agent: the model the adapter runs, in place of its pinned default; an adapter with no model flag refuses one.

records.description: records: the directory the adopter's harness writes its sealed records to, relative to the evaluation folder (POSIX, with no "." or ".." segment): evaluator-configuration.json, and one directory per probe holding its SealedRunRecord files and, optionally, isolation-manifest.json.

tiers.description: The CI tiers this evaluation takes part in (AD-10).

strengthFloor.description: Minimum catch rate per probe class, from 0 to 1.

RegistryEntry.description: One command a run may spawn. interfaceId and executable key it the way eval-quality's command target policy keys an authorization; the pair is unique within the registry.

kind.description: The interface kind this entry serves: cli, the default when absent.

interfaceId.description: The logical interface identifier the contract names (a kebab-case slug).

executable.description: The logical executable a contract operation's invocation names (a kebab-case slug).

target.description: What the adapter spawns: a POSIX path relative to the root the runtime resolves the registry against (the evaluated project), or a bare command name the adapter resolves through its own PATH. Never absolute, and never with a "." or ".." segment, an empty segment, a trailing slash, or a control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character, so a registry cannot point outside the project it describes.

subcommandPaths.description: The exact subcommand paths this target may be invoked with; an empty inner array authorizes invoking it with no subcommand.

artifacts.description: Default path of each artifact identifier the contract declares for this target, relative to the run's working directory: POSIX, never absolute, never with a "." or ".." segment, an empty segment, a trailing slash, or a control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character, so a registry cannot read a file outside the run back as evidence. A caller may override a path per run.

environmentKeys.description: Environment keys a request may carry into the process. PATH is never one: target may name a bare command, and a declared PATH would choose which binary runs.

maxElapsedMs.description: Wall-clock ceiling for one invocation, in milliseconds. A caller may lower it per run; the ceiling is the most any run gets. At most 2147483647, the longest delay one timer holds, which eval-quality's command target policy also refuses to exceed.

maxOutputBytes.description: Ceiling on each captured stream and each artifact read back, in bytes. Defaults to 8 MiB. A caller may lower it per run; the ceiling is the most any run gets.

infrastructureExitCodes.description: The exit codes by which this target reports that it could not run: a launch, configuration, transport, timeout or parse failure, or a crash. tea-evaluate check refuses a defect signature or manifestation witness that could hold on an observation carrying one of these codes and no output (AD-7). Empty when the target reports no such failure through its exit code.

McpRegistryEntry.description: One stdio MCP tool server a run may start (AD-4: a tool-use target whose interface is mcp). The runtime turns each into an McpTargetAuthorization of eval-quality's default-deny McpTargetPolicy, validated through its parseMcpTargetPolicy, for the workspace each call runs in, and calls the server through its createMcpAdapter: one session per call, the server started with targetArgs, working in that workspace, with the host's values for environmentKeys as its environment. eval-quality's policy admits one entry per interfaceId, since for this mechanism the interface is the server.

kind.description: mcp: this entry is a tool server.

interfaceId.description: The logical interface identifier the contract names for the server (a kebab-case slug).

target.description: What the adapter starts: a POSIX path relative to the root the runtime resolves the registry against (the evaluated project, so the path lands in the workspace), or a bare command name the adapter resolves through the host PATH. Never absolute, and never with a "." or ".." segment, an empty segment, a trailing slash, or a control character (C0, DEL or C1), a line or paragraph separator, or a bidirectional formatting character.

targetArgs.description: The argument vector the server starts with, passed as an array so no value is joined into a shell string; a relative path in it resolves against the workspace, the server's working directory, so every file the server runs is the workspace's copy. No argument is an absolute path, carries one after an = sign, names a file: URL, or has a ".." segment, since any of them would run or read the adopter's live tree in place of the workspace (AD-8). Empty starts target with no arguments.

tools.description: The tools this server may be asked to call, in its own spelling, compared literally by eval-quality: a call naming a tool absent from this list is denied (tool-not-authorized) before the server starts, even when the server publishes it. eval-quality's parseMcpTargetPolicy decides which names are valid.

environmentKeys.description: Environment keys whose host values the server starts with (its serverEnvironment), over the host PATH; a tool call carries only its arguments, so a server needing a credential receives it here. PATH is never one: target may name a bare command, and a declared PATH would choose which binary runs.

maxElapsedMs.description: Wall-clock ceiling for one call, in milliseconds: the server's start, the initialize handshake, the tool call and its teardown. At most 2147483647, the longest delay one timer holds.

maxOutputBytes.description: Ceiling on the bytes the server writes on stdout and, separately, on stderr in one call, in bytes. Defaults to 8 MiB.
